announcements.text: Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Aerospace Systems. Melbourne, Florida, is awarded a not-to-exceed $1,196,000,000 cost, no fee undefinitized contract for the production, delivery, and associated support for three E-2D Advanced Hawkeye Block II aircraft for the Navy. Work will be performed in Melbourne, Florida (29.88%); St. Augustine, Florida (17.68%); Liverpool, New York (13.85%); Indianapolis, Indiana (4.95%); Largo, Florida (3.66%); San Leandro, California (2.52%); Woodland Hills, California (2.42%); Aire-sur-l’Adour, France (2.09%); Rolling Meadows, Illinois (1.72%); Wimborne Minster, Dorset, United Kingdom (0.01%); and various locations within the continental U.S. (21.22%), and is expected to be completed in December 2031. Fiscal 2026 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $583,394,000 will be obligated at the time of award. This contract was not competed in accordance with 10 U.S. Code 2304(c)(1). Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity (N0001926C1017).

announcements.text: Raytheon, Tucson, Arizona, is awarded an $18,977,361 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-26-C-5434) for technical and design agent engineering in support of the Evolved SeaSparrow Missile and NATO SeaSparrow Missile Systems programs. Work will be performed in Tucson, Arizona (85%); and Portsmouth, Rhode Island (15%), and is expected to be completed by December 2030. This modification combines purchases for the U.S. Navy (36%) and the governments of Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Türkiye (under Memorandum of Agreements (63%)); and Japan (under Foreign Military Sales (FMS) cases (1%)). Fiscal 2025 other customer funds in the amount of $7,697,880 (36%); fiscal 2026 other customer funds in the amount of $5,295,484 (24%); fiscal 2026 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $ 2,429,221 (11%); fiscal 2025 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,766,007 (8%); fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,736,477 (8%); fiscal 2025 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,122,366 (5%); fiscal 2024 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $530,573 (2%); fiscal 2024 other customer funds in the amount of $433,289 (2%); fiscal 2026 FMS Japan funds in the amount of $251,165 (1%); fiscal 2022 other customer funds in the amount of $150,000 (1%); fiscal 2024 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $111,656 (1%); and fiscal 2023 other customer funds in the amount of $83,000 (<1%); fiscal 2025 other procurement (Navy) $20,569 (<1%) will be obligated at time of award, of which $642,229 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: Laboratory Corp. of America, Burlington, North Carolina, was awarded $364,702,439 for a single-award, indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity contract utilizing firm-fixed-price task orders to provide the Defense Health Agency with commercial clinical reference laboratory testing services across both the continental United States and outside the continental United States. This competitive, non-personal services contract will support military beneficiaries worldwide by processing vital diagnostic laboratory tests that military medical treatment facilities currently lack the capability or capacity to execute in-house. This strategic sourcing initiative was competitively solicited under solicitation number HT001526RE001, which was posted to SAM.gov on May 12, 2026, and closed on June 1, 2026. The contract features a five-year base period followed by a five-year option period, establishing a worldwide performance location with an ultimate completion date of July 9, 2036. No fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds are being obligated at time of award. The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity, Enterprise Medical Services Contracting Division, San Antonio, Texas, is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: Synensys LLC, Peachtree, Georgia, is awarded $9,391,875 for a firm-fixed price option modification (P00002) to a previously awarded contract (HT001125C0076) for Defense Health Agency (DHA) Deputy Assistant Director - Medical Affairs Patient Safety Program for military medical treatment facilities services. The contract encompasses patient safety personnel at numerous military hospitals and clinics coupled with training materials to foster a workplace-based safety cultural transformation, guided by experts in patient safety at DHA. Services include expertise and experience required by patient safety specialists, patient safety assistant coordinators, and patient safety data analysts at both inpatient and outpatient facilities. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds are obligated to exercise and fully fund Option One for 12 months from Aug. 1, 2026, to July 31, 2027. The places of performance are military hospitals and clinics inside and outside the continental U.S. DHA, Professional Services Contracting Division, Falls Church, Virginia, is the contracting activity.
